description: For each account scope, count the distinct orders that have risk/margin records and link to users, so each order counts once. Report the count, its share of the total across scopes, and its ratio to the average count across scopes.

b.request: For each account scope, count distinct orders linked to a user in that scope and matched to at least one risk/margin record; report the scope, the order count, its unrounded share of the total count across scopes, and its unrounded ratio to the average count per scope
b.sql: WITH scope_counts AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS scope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.userlink = u.userstamp AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM riskandmargin r WHERE r.ordervault = o.recordvault) WHERE u.acctscope IS NOT NULL GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT scope, order_count, order_count::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(order_count) OVER (), 0) AS share_of_total, order_count::numeric / NULLIF(AVG(order_count) OVER (), 0) AS ratio_to_average FROM scope_counts ORDER BY scope;

c.request: Matching risk/margin records to their orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and orders to their users (`userlink` = `userstamp`), and ignoring anything that doesn't match: for each account scope (`users.acctscope`), how many risk/margin-matched orders are there? Show the scope, that count, its share of the total across all scopes, and the count divided by the average count per scope, without rounding. For each account scope, count the distinct orders that have risk/margin records and link to users, so each order counts once. Report the count, its share of the total across scopes, and its ratio to the average count across scopes.
c.sql: WITH scope_counts AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count::numeric / AVG(order_count) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM scope_counts ORDER BY acctscope;

a.request: Match risk/margin records to orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and orders to users (`userlink` = `userstamp`), dropping anything without a match. For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), give the scope, the number of distinct orders (an order with two risk/margin records counts once), that number as a fraction of the total across all scopes, and that number divided by the average of those numbers across scopes, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH scope_counts AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, order_count::numeric / AVG(order_count) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM scope_counts

d.request: For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), count distinct orders that match a risk/margin record (`ordervault = recordvault`) and a user (`userlink = userstamp`), excluding unmatched records so each order counts once. Report the scope, count, its share of the total across all scopes, and its ratio to the average count per scope, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH scope_counts AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.userlink = u.userstamp JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count::numeric / AVG(order_count) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM scope_counts ORDER BY acctscope;
